judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports hit all four expectations and are largely comparable; Report 2 is marginally stronger on the doc-update policy by explicitly endorsing a going-forward same-commit rule.

report_1.evidence: New provider calls belong in `medibill/backend/app/billing/gateway.py`. ... A refund would be a new accessor there, e.g. `refund(...)`. ... `medibill/backend/app/api/invoices.py` ... builds `chargekit.Client(...)` ... `medibill/backend/app/workers/dunning.py` ... constructs a fresh `chargekit.Client(...)` ... `app/billing/errors.py` as the only sanctioned exception (it imports just the SDK's exception types

report_2.evidence: New refund calls should live in `medibill/backend/app/billing/gateway.py`, as a new accessor function (e.g. `refund(...)`) ... `backend/app/api/invoices.py` — imports `chargekit` directly (line 4) and constructs its own client ... `backend/app/workers/dunning.py` — imports `chargekit` directly (line 2) and constructs a fresh client ... `errors.py` (which only re-exports the SDK's exception types, `errors.py:6-9`) as the sole exception

report_1.evidence: the response model `InvoiceOut` also carries `external_ref` (`backend/app/models/invoice.py:22`, serialized at lines 26-28, populated in `invoices.py:17`, backed by `migrations/0006_add_invoice_external_ref.sql`). Six fields, not five

report_2.evidence: `InvoiceOut` has **six** fields — those five plus `external_ref: str | None` (`backend/app/models/invoice.py:16-22`) ... The field was added in commit `c23da88` (MEDB-214), together with migration `0006_add_invoice_external_ref.sql`

report_1.evidence: It should be corrected **before or together with the refund implementation — in the same reviewed change series, not deferred**. ... The history argues against "update it later" ... Deferring again just extends a demonstrated drift pattern.

report_2.evidence: It should be corrected to match reality **before any refund code is written** — as the first commit of the refund work (or an immediately-preceding standalone commit), not "eventually." ... Going forward, treat drift as a merge-blocking bug: any commit that changes the invoice response shape, the webhook set, or the provider boundary must update this doc in the same commit.

report_1.evidence: drop the hard-coded count. "Handles 4 webhook event types" is the most fragile possible phrasing — a count plus a closed list, in prose, far from the code — and it failed in exactly the expected way. Restate it to name the source of truth and describe behavior

report_2.evidence: drop the hardcoded count entirely. A literal "handles 4" is guaranteed to go stale the next time anyone adds an `if` branch ... Restate it as a pointer to the single source of truth
